title: Authentication
summary: How logins work (authentication = who you are, authorization = what you may do, 401 vs 403, JWTs), then Claude Code gives your app real email accounts, with the database's RLS rules deciding who sees what.
goal: Replace Myflix's anonymous sign-in with real Register, Log in and Log out, so each account sees only its own lists and comments, enforced by RLS with auth.uid().

Homework Part I, priority 2: 50 steps of the FreeCodeCamp Python certification
Homework Part II, priority 1: your own app: add authentication (lecture steps 4–8) with proper RLS rules
Homework Part II, priority 2: Netflix Clone IV: the same steps on your Netflix clone
Homework Part II, priority 3: 100 steps of the FreeCodeCamp JavaScript certification

This prompt is a suggestion, not from the lecture.

steps.title: Back up, then drop the tables
steps.detail: Lecture step 4. Turn Confirm email off first (Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Email → Confirm email off → Save; development only). Export each table to CSV (Table Editor → table → Export → Export to CSV) into supabase/backups/, e.g. lists_backup_2026-10-19.csv. Your tables: profiles, genres, shows, list_entries, list_comments, lists, list_items. Your functions: handle_new_user and set_updated_at. Authentication → Users must be empty, so delete your anonymous test users. Then in Claude (root, /model → Opus) paste the instructor prompt with your tables in place of (LIST YOUR TABLES).
steps.code: I backed up all my tables to CSV in supabase/backups/. Using the Supabase MCP, drop my app's tables (LIST YOUR TABLES) and any functions I made for them, so the project is empty. Show me the SQL first and wait for my approval.
steps.doneWhen: 7 CSVs are in supabase/backups/, Authentication → Users is empty, and Table Editor shows no tables after you approved the SQL.

steps.title: Run the Supabase prompt
steps.detail: Lecture step 5, same session. Good answers for you: your users table is profiles. Its id IS the auth.users id, and handle_new_user / on_auth_user_created already fill it in; keep that. Every user_id defaults to auth.uid() (it already does). Every policy is to authenticated and allows only your own rows ("tasks" means your list entries, comments, lists and your own shows). Genres and catalog shows (no created_by) are shared, like Ticked's tags: any logged-in user can read them. The catalog seed is fine to reload, but don't re-import rows that belonged to anonymous users: they have no login. Update supabase/schema.sql when done. At each pause, check Database → Triggers (on_auth_user_created), Authentication → Policies (auth.uid() = user_id, no "dev:" rules) and Table Editor (RLS on).
steps.code:

I would like you to take a look at the following resources:

1. User Journey can be found: front-end/app_outline/user_journey.md
2. The current supabase schema is as follows: supabase/schema.sql

Using these resources as context I would like you to conduct the following:

2. ensure proper RLS policies are set where a user can only view the tasks they own.

After conducting each action, pause and ask for confirmation that your actions worked correctly before proceeding to the next step.

Do you have any questions before executing this task?

steps.title: Run the Vite + React prompt
steps.detail: Lecture step 6. Fill in your URL (no /rest/v1) and publishable key from front-end/.env.local. Your variable is VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY; keep that name. Good answers: a Log in page and a Register page; every other page needs a logged-in user. Show the user's name and a Log out button in the header. Keep the Supabase calls in src/lib/. Different for you: remove the signInAnonymously() call in src/lib/session.js (that's your "demo user"). Myflix has no React Router yet, so Claude may ask how to show the new pages. Never use the secret key.
steps.code:
Utilizing the following resources:

- Supabase db schema: supabase/schema.sql
- user journey: front-end/app_outline/user_journey.md
- Project API url: https://your-project-id.supabase.co
- Project API Key: your-publishable-key

I would like you to update the functionality for the User Authentication process. Consider the following actions a user can take:

- Register: A brand new user can sign up for our application and interact with our site.
- Log In: A returning user can interact with our site and ONLY their corresponding data
- Log out: A logged in user can end their session and exit our website while removing their credentials from the front-end code.
- User Confirmation: While logged in we need to have a way of confirming who the user is
    - while logged in if the user refreshes the browser, we should be able of leveraging the current credentials to recover the logged in `user` and their corresponding`data`

Each of these actions should be an independent phase. Utilize playwright to ensure completion of each phase prior to moving on to the next one.

Do you have any questions before completing these actions?
steps.doneWhen: Claude reports all four phases (Register, Log in, Log out, refresh) passed in Playwright.

steps.title: Prove it with two accounts
steps.detail: Lecture step 7. Register account A in a normal window and add a show to My List. Register account B in a private window. Then you can turn off Anonymous sign-ins (Authentication → Sign In / Providers), so nobody gets in without an account.
steps.doneWhen: B can't see A's list. Refreshing A keeps you logged in, and Log out goes back to Log in. Table Editor → profiles has one row per account, and each list_entries.user_id matches its owner.

concepts.meaning: Proving who you are, like logging in with email and password.
Deciding what a known user may do, like only seeing their own list.
401 means "I don't know who you are"; 403 means "I know you, but you're not allowed."
A signed token in three parts (header, payload, signature) that tells the server who you are; anyone can read it, so no secrets in it.
The access token is short-lived (about 1 hour); the refresh token quietly gets a new one so you stay logged in.
A Postgres function that returns the logged-in user's id from the JWT, so RLS rules can say "only your rows".
Database rules that filter every request by who is asking.
Database code that runs by itself on an event, like making a profiles row when a new account signs up.
What Myflix uses now: a throwaway account per browser with no email, so it can't log in again on another device.
